dedupe_keys.name: ambon city indonesia system dynamics evaluation of municipal solid waste policy scenarios 2026 to 2035

description: This case study tests policies for meeting Ambon City's target of managing all municipal solid waste by 2029. Sukmawati Lapele and Dwi Handayani of the Islamic University of Indonesia built a system dynamics model in Powersim Studio 10 that projects waste generation and management performance from 2026 to 2035, verified its structure and checked that it reproduces past behaviour, and published the study in the International Journal of Current Science Research and Review in 2026. Scenarios compare business as usual with upstream reduce, reuse and recycle measures, collection and transport expansion and an integrated waste processing facility (TPST) before landfill. The article is free to read online in an open access journal. Coverage is the city of Ambon in Maluku province. Caveats: the model and data are not published, and results rest on assumed growth in management capacity. Business as usual misses the 2029 target; the integrated scenario works best, with a 30 percent community-based 3R target needing management capacity to grow 38.43 percent a year, which lowers the required yearly growth in collection and transport capacity from 8.94 to 5.50 percent, and a 74 tonne per day processing facility greatly cuts landfilled waste. Simulation uses: capacity growth rates and scenario structure for waste system planning models in island cities. Related records: the China domestic waste system dynamics study (case_study-china-domestic-waste-management-system-dynamics-cost-benefit-2100) uses the same method at national scale.
